pages.title: Complement, AND, OR and precedence
pages.text: A complement means NOT: A̅ is one when A is zero.
pages.remember: By De Morgan's law it equals (NOT A) OR (NOT B), for every input combination.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A complement means NOT: A̅ is one when A is zero. A·B denotes AND and A+B denotes OR in Boolean notation. Parentheses group terms, and multiplication-like AND normally has precedence over OR. De Morgan's laws describe how an inverted group changes operations, letting engineers transform logic without changing the truth table.
Where this model can mislead you
Boolean '+' is not integer sum: 1+1=1 in Boolean OR. Confusing this with binary addition causes incorrect troubleshooting and truth-table results.

Compute B·C=0 first, then F=0+0=0.
Convert NOT(A·B) into (NOT A)+(NOT B) and verify by writing all four possible input combinations.
worked.conclusion: By De Morgan's law it equals (NOT A) OR (NOT B), for every input combination.

reflection.ask: How does NOT(A AND B) relate to two inverted inputs?

pages.title: XOR, XNOR and parity checking
pages.text: Exclusive OR, written XOR, is true when two binary inputs differ.
pages.remember: Because XOR tests whether inputs differ; equal inputs produce zero, unlike inclusive OR.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

Exclusive OR, written XOR, is true when two binary inputs differ. XNOR is true when they match. Unlike ordinary OR, XOR is false for 1,1. XOR is useful for detecting change, equality differences, parity bits and arithmetic carry logic. These are separate functions from a displayed bit pattern.
Where this model can mislead you
A parity check can detect many single-bit errors but cannot reliably detect every multiple-bit error. It is an error-detection clue, not proof of data integrity.

worked.heading: Reason it through · XOR, XNOR and parity checking
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: Construct XOR rows 00→0,01→1,10→1,11→0.
Given data 1,0,1,1, compute even-parity bit by XORing the four data bits: 1 XOR 0 XOR 1 XOR 1 =1.
Appending a parity 1 makes the total number of ones even.
worked.conclusion: Because XOR tests whether inputs differ; equal inputs produce zero, unlike inclusive OR.

reflection.ask: Why is XOR zero when both inputs are one?
reflection.answer: Because XOR tests whether inputs differ; equal inputs produce zero, unlike inclusive OR.

pages.title: Combinational equations to logic gates
pages.text: A combinational circuit's outputs depend on present inputs, not stored history.
pages.remember: Zero AND one gives zero; NOT zero is one; OR therefore produces one.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A combinational circuit's outputs depend on present inputs, not stored history. To implement an equation, separate NOT, AND and OR stages and trace intermediate signals. An output can sometimes be implemented with NAND or NOR gates only, because these families are functionally complete. Explain each gate with its truth relationship before counting parts.
Where this model can mislead you
Propagation delay means a physical combinational circuit can glitch during input transitions even if its steady-state Boolean truth table is correct.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Combinational equations to logic gates
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: Implement F=(A AND B) OR (NOT C).
Label intermediate X=A·B and Y=NOT C; send X and Y to an OR.
Then build a truth table to check the circuit instead of trusting its drawing alone.
worked.conclusion: Zero AND one gives zero; NOT zero is one; OR therefore produces one.

reflection.ask: For F=A·B+NOT C, what is F at A=1,B=0,C=0?
reflection.answer: Zero AND one gives zero; NOT zero is one; OR therefore produces one.

pages.title: Karnaugh thinking and Boolean simplification
pages.text: Equivalent truth-table outputs can often be implemented by fewer gates.
pages.remember: B OR NOT B is always one, so A AND one equals A.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

Equivalent truth-table outputs can often be implemented by fewer gates. Factoring and Boolean identities are methods for simplification. Absorption A+A·B=A says that once A is true the extra AND term does not change the result. For a small number of inputs, Karnaugh maps group adjacent ones to expose repeated terms.
Where this model can mislead you
A simplified gate count is not automatically the fastest, lowest-power or safest physical implementation. Fan-out, timing glitches, wiring and signal loading still matter.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Karnaugh thinking and Boolean simplification
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: Start with F=A·B + A·NOT B.
Factor A: F=A(B+NOT B)=A·1=A.
Verify with A=0,B=0/1 and A=1,B=0/1.
Four truth-table rows establish that a single wire carrying A gives the same steady logic answer.
worked.conclusion: B OR NOT B is always one, so A AND one equals A.

reflection.ask: Why does A·B + A·NOT B reduce to A?
reflection.answer: B OR NOT B is always one, so A AND one equals A.

pages.title: Bit width, signed values and masks
pages.text: Bits are interpreted by convention: unsigned values use all positions for magnitude, while two's-complement signed values reserve a negative weight for the most significant bit.
pages.remember: The bit pattern is identical; the unsigned or signed two's-complement interpretation changes its numerical meaning.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

Bits are interpreted by convention: unsigned values use all positions for magnitude, while two's-complement signed values reserve a negative weight for the most significant bit. A mask is a bit pattern used with AND to select fields or OR to set chosen positions. A register's written bit pattern requires its datasheet meaning, not merely its decimal value.
Where this model can mislead you
Do not sign-extend an unsigned field or assume a register is eight bits just because an example is. Reserved fields, access permissions and atomicity rules come from the actual peripheral manual.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Bit width, signed values and masks
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: Interpret 11111110₂ as unsigned 254 and as signed 8-bit two's complement −2.
To test whether bit 3 of 00101000₂ is set, AND with 00001000₂; the nonzero result means the bit is one.
Note that bit zero is the least significant bit.
worked.conclusion: The bit pattern is identical; the unsigned or signed two's-complement interpretation changes its numerical meaning.

reflection.ask: How can one eight-bit pattern mean both 254 and −2?
reflection.answer: The bit pattern is identical; the unsigned or signed two's-complement interpretation changes its numerical meaning.

pages.title: Truth-table verification and fault diagnosis
pages.text: A technician checks logic by specifying the expected conditions, finding the signal path and comparing observed states with the relevant truth table.
pages.remember: Because the inputs may not satisfy valid HIGH thresholds or the power/reference may be wrong; verify those first.
pages.sourceLesson: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A technician checks logic by specifying the expected conditions, finding the signal path and comparing observed states with the relevant truth table. Begin with valid supply, ground, stable inputs and logic family thresholds. A state mismatch may come from a wrong equation, floating input, broken connection, propagation timing or failed gate.
Where this model can mislead you

A DMM is suitable for static checks but can conceal short pulses and glitches. Unknown high-energy circuitry is outside this simulated beginner exercise; use properly rated instruments and trained supervision.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Truth-table verification and fault diagnosis
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: Given an AND gate that must output one for inputs A=1 and B=1, observe output zero.
Check the IC supply and input-pin voltages first.
If B is actually below its defined VIH threshold, the gate may be behaving correctly; fix the input problem before condemning the chip.
worked.conclusion: Because the inputs may not satisfy valid HIGH thresholds or the power/reference may be wrong; verify those first.

reflection.ask: Why shouldn't you replace an AND gate immediately after reading an unexpected low output?
reflection.answer: Because the inputs may not satisfy valid HIGH thresholds or the power/reference may be wrong; verify those first.

examples.title: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

detail.problem: Convert binary 1011 0110 to hex and decimal.
steps: Group into nibbles: 1011 and 0110.
1011₂ = B₁₆; 0110₂ = 6₁₆, so B6₁₆.
detail.answer: B6 hex and 182 decimal.
detail.transfer: A register value shown as 0xB6 can be decoded bit-by-bit using the same conversion.

examples.title: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

detail.problem: A register reads 0xB6. Convert it to binary and identify whether bits 7, 5, 3, and 0 are set.
steps: Bit positions from left are 7..0: 1 0 1 1 0 1 1 0.
Bits 7 and 5 are set; bit 3 is 0; bit 0 is 0.
detail.answer: 0xB6=10110110; bits 7 and 5 are set, bits 3 and 0 are clear.
detail.meaning: Hex-to-bit conversion is the basis of register masks and digital bus interpretation.

examples.title: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

detail.problem: An 8-bit unsigned counter holding 255 is incremented once.
steps: Eight unsigned bits represent 0 through 255.
255 is binary 11111111.
Adding one produces 1 00000000; only eight stored bits remain.
The stored result wraps to 0 in unsigned arithmetic.
detail.answer: 0, due to modulo-256 unsigned wrap.
detail.transfer: A wrapped timer/counter can break comparisons unless rollover is handled intentionally.

examples.title: Computer blocks, representation, memory, and the build path

detail.problem: A small C program compiles each source file successfully but the final build reports 'undefined reference to read_sensor'.
steps: Compilation succeeded, so the syntax in the individual source files is acceptable enough to produce objects.
The undefined reference appears during linking because a required symbol declaration/call exists but the linker cannot find a matching definition in linked objects/libraries.
Check whether the implementation file is included in the build, symbol spelling/signature matches, and the correct library/object is linked.
Do not troubleshoot runtime sensor wiring until an executable image exists.
detail.answer: Treat this as a link-stage dependency/symbol problem, not a runtime hardware failure.
detail.meaning: Identifying the build stage narrows the search space before any code or hardware change.

guided.text: Convert decimal 45 to binary and hex, then convert 0x3C back to binary and decimal.
Build a truth table for Y=(A AND B) OR (NOT C). Verify all eight combinations.
A D flip-flop samples on a rising edge. Explain what setup/hold means and why changing D at the same instant as the clock edge can produce an uncertain result.
Classify five failures as compile, link, load/program, or runtime: syntax error, undefined reference, programmer cannot connect, program hard-faults, missing header declaration warning.
Draw CPU, RAM, flash/nonvolatile storage, and peripheral I/O blocks. Trace what happens from power-up to executing an instruction that reads an input.
Explain a PLC scan using a start/stop input and motor output, then identify what field measurement is needed to prove the output actually energized.

teachBack: Explain how one byte can be written in binary, hex, and decimal, then use a small gate expression and a flip-flop to explain the difference between combinational and sequential logic.

questions.prompt: What is the hexadecimal representation of decimal 10?
questions.explanation: 10 decimal = A hexadecimal. Each hex place is a power of 16; A through F represent 10 through 15..

questions.prompt: What is the hexadecimal representation of decimal 18?
questions.explanation: 18 decimal = 12 hexadecimal. Each hex place is a power of 16; A through F represent 10 through 15..

questions.prompt: What is the hexadecimal representation of decimal 25?
questions.explanation: 25 decimal = 19 hexadecimal. Each hex place is a power of 16; A through F represent 10 through 15..

questions.prompt: What is the hexadecimal representation of decimal 42?
questions.explanation: 42 decimal = 2A hexadecimal. Each hex place is a power of 16; A through F represent 10 through 15..

questions.prompt: What is the hexadecimal representation of decimal 63?
questions.explanation: 63 decimal = 3F hexadecimal. Each hex place is a power of 16; A through F represent 10 through 15..

questions.prompt: What is the hexadecimal representation of decimal 85?
questions.explanation: 85 decimal = 55 hexadecimal. Each hex place is a power of 16; A through F represent 10 through 15..

questions.prompt: What is the hexadecimal representation of decimal 127?
questions.explanation: 127 decimal = 7F hexadecimal. Each hex place is a power of 16; A through F represent 10 through 15..

questions.prompt: What is the hexadecimal representation of decimal 170?
questions.explanation: 170 decimal = AA hexadecimal. Each hex place is a power of 16; A through F represent 10 through 15..

questions.prompt: What decimal value does binary 1011 represent?
questions.explanation: Its place values give 8 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 11.

questions.prompt: What is decimal 10 in four-bit binary?
questions.explanation: Correct. 8 + 2 = 10, so bits 3 and 1 are set: 1010.

questions.prompt: What is binary 110101₂ in decimal?
Which hexadecimal number is binary 11101010₂?
questions.explanation: 1110 is E and 1010 is A; combined EA.

questions.prompt: A fan runs only when both ENABLE and HOT equal 1. Which Boolean function is correct?
questions.explanation: Both asserted signals are required, giving AND.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to NOT(A AND B)?
questions.explanation: De Morgan's law complements both inputs and changes AND to OR.

questions.prompt: What is XOR output for input A=1,B=1?
questions.explanation: XOR tests difference; equal inputs give 0.

questions.prompt: Eight-bit 11111110₂ can mean which pair depending on interpretation?
questions.explanation: Unsigned adds weights to 254; eight-bit two’s complement gives −2.

questions.prompt: For an AND output stuck LOW with two intended HIGH inputs, what should be verified first?
choices: Measure actual input voltage against required thresholds and check supply

pages.title: Logic gates as real electronic building blocks
pages.text: An electronic logic gate uses transistors to produce output voltage ranges that represent true and false.
pages.remember: It makes a NAND function: the output is the complement of A AND B.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

An electronic logic gate uses transistors to produce output voltage ranges that represent true and false. AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR and XNOR describe different mappings, each represented by a symbol and truth table. A symbol's inversion bubble means logical NOT at that terminal. Logical behavior describes stable states and does not specify propagation delay.
Where this model can mislead you
Gate symbols can be rotated or use alternative conventions. Always check polarity marks and manufacturer datasheet pin numbering; never guess pinout from the drawing.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Logic gates as real electronic building blocks
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: Compare NAND and AND for inputs 1,1: AND yields 1, NAND yields 0.
For 1,0: AND yields 0, NAND yields 1.
Explain why a NAND's output bubble matters even if the triangle or body is drawn differently by a publisher.
worked.conclusion: It makes a NAND function: the output is the complement of A AND B.

reflection.ask: What does an output inversion bubble add to an AND symbol?
reflection.answer: It makes a NAND function: the output is the complement of A AND B.

pages.title: Truth tables as a test plan
pages.text: A truth table lists every input combination and the output expected for each.
pages.remember: Sixteen, because each of the four independent inputs doubles the combinations: 2⁴=16.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A truth table lists every input combination and the output expected for each. For n independent inputs, there are 2ⁿ rows. This helps distinguish an OR from XOR or a NAND from NOR without relying on loose language such as 'both high'. In real troubleshooting, use the table to pick useful static cases.
Where this model can mislead you
A truth table covers stable logical combinations; it does not reveal momentary glitches or input setup/hold violations during transitions.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Truth tables as a test plan
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: For three inputs A,B,C there are 2³=8 rows.
Compare the row 110 with the gate stages A AND B then OR C.
worked.conclusion: Sixteen, because each of the four independent inputs doubles the combinations: 2⁴=16.

reflection.ask: How many rows are needed for a complete four-input combinational truth table?
reflection.answer: Sixteen, because each of the four independent inputs doubles the combinations: 2⁴=16.

pages.title: Active-low control and gate inversions
pages.text: An active-low signal asserts its function at logical zero, often written with an overbar or suffix such as _N.
pages.remember: The chip-select function is asserted because the suffix indicates an active-low control.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

An active-low signal asserts its function at logical zero, often written with an overbar or suffix such as _N. This naming affects debugging: a /RESET line driven low requests reset. NAND/NOR gates make sense when negative logic is explicit, while a technician must distinguish a logically asserted control from a high voltage.
Where this model can mislead you
Active-low symbols and names are conventions; datasheet electrical thresholds still determine a valid zero. A low on an unknown pin may also reflect a short or power-off state.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Active-low control and gate inversions
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: A chip-select named CS_N is measured at 0.1 V and the device's input-low limit is 0.8 V.
CS_N is asserted.
A technician who assumes 'low=inactive' would misdiagnose a peripheral that is intentionally selected.
Draw a timing line showing selected low and deselected high.
worked.conclusion: The chip-select function is asserted because the suffix indicates an active-low control.

reflection.ask: What does CS_N=0 usually mean in a correctly powered device?
reflection.answer: The chip-select function is asserted because the suffix indicates an active-low control.

pages.title: Logic families and valid voltage margins
pages.text: TTL and CMOS are families of circuit implementations with different electrical input thresholds, drive behavior and power characteristics.
pages.remember: The difference between guaranteed minimum output HIGH voltage and the receiver's required minimum input HIGH threshold.
pages.sourceLesson: Real logic levels, pull resistors, debounce, and measurement

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

TTL and CMOS are families of circuit implementations with different electrical input thresholds, drive behavior and power characteristics. Logic one is a region above VIH(min), while logic zero is below VIL(max). Between these limits the input may be indeterminate. Output VOH(min) and VOL(max) must fit the receiving circuit's required ranges with noise margin.
Where this model can mislead you
Input thresholds differ across voltage supplies, temperature and part families. The terms TTL and CMOS alone do not replace the specific datasheet tables.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Logic families and valid voltage margins
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: Suppose an output guarantees VOH ≥2.4 V and the receiving input requires VIH ≥2.0 V; the guaranteed HIGH margin is at least 0.4 V.
If a different receiver requires 3.5 V, that output cannot be assumed compatible.
Check both families rather than comparing only nominal supplies.
worked.conclusion: The difference between guaranteed minimum output HIGH voltage and the receiver's required minimum input HIGH threshold.

reflection.ask: What is a high-level noise margin?
reflection.answer: The difference between guaranteed minimum output HIGH voltage and the receiver's required minimum input HIGH threshold.

pages.text: A seven-segment display uses labeled segments to represent characters; common-anode and common-cathode constructions require different drive arrangements.
pages.remember: An LED's current rises sharply with voltage, so resistance or a controlled driver prevents overcurrent.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A seven-segment display uses labeled segments to represent characters; common-anode and common-cathode constructions require different drive arrangements. A display driver translates a code into segment drive currents, and resistors or current-regulated outputs limit LED current. Multiplexing scans digits fast enough to appear stable while reducing wiring, but increases timing requirements.
Where this model can mislead you
GPIO current limits may prohibit direct display driving. Common-anode/cathode wiring, polarity, peak multiplex current and brightness need the actual device specifications.

pages.title: Logic probes and meaningful signal states
pages.text: A logic probe indicates whether a selected point is low, high or pulsing according to its own threshold and pulse-detection scheme.
pages.remember: The pin's active polarity, expected operating state, logic thresholds and reference connection.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A logic probe indicates whether a selected point is low, high or pulsing according to its own threshold and pulse-detection scheme. It is useful for simple powered digital checks, but not a universal voltmeter. Establish probe supply/reference and rated logic family before touching a circuit, and inspect the pin function in the schematic.
Where this model can mislead you

A logic probe can miss narrow pulses and can load sensitive nodes. Some instruments have family selection and specific safe-input limits; never assume protection against mains or high-energy equipment.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Logic probes and meaningful signal states
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: An enable line appears low on a digital logic probe.
First identify whether ENABLE_N is active-low and whether the measured voltage satisfies a valid VIL range.
Check a nearby known clock point for activity before deciding that the IC is frozen.
worked.conclusion: The pin's active polarity, expected operating state, logic thresholds and reference connection.

reflection.ask: What must you know before calling a probe's LOW light a malfunction?
reflection.answer: The pin's active polarity, expected operating state, logic thresholds and reference connection.

pages.title: Ports, direction control and register behavior
pages.text: A general-purpose digital pin is configured by control registers and may be an input, push-pull output, open-drain output or peripheral-function pin.
pages.remember: The pin may still be configured as input, controlled by another peripheral, or electrically loaded or faulted.
pages.sourceLesson: Bit fields, ports, processors, and stored state

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A general-purpose digital pin is configured by control registers and may be an input, push-pull output, open-drain output or peripheral-function pin. Pull resistors and alternate-function multiplexers affect its observed level. A physical pin set as input often does not drive a defined voltage unless an external or internal pull supplies it.
Where this model can mislead you
Registers and pin functions vary by MCU. Some input reads reflect the physical pin, while output latches and alternate functions behave differently; consult the specific reference manual.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Ports, direction control and register behavior
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: An MCU code writes 1 to an output-data register but its pin remains low.
Check whether the pin was configured as an output, whether an alternate peripheral owns it, and whether a short or overloaded driver exists.
The written register value alone does not prove pin voltage.
worked.conclusion: The pin may still be configured as input, controlled by another peripheral, or electrically loaded or faulted.

reflection.ask: Why might writing 1 to a GPIO latch not make the pin HIGH?
reflection.answer: The pin may still be configured as input, controlled by another peripheral, or electrically loaded or faulted.

pages.title: Sequential circuits remember past conditions
pages.text: Combinational logic depends only on current inputs; sequential logic depends on an internal state remembered from earlier events.
pages.remember: Q is stored and updates on the specified clock edge, not on every change of D.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

Combinational logic depends only on current inputs; sequential logic depends on an internal state remembered from earlier events. Latches are level-sensitive in common designs, while flip-flops are generally controlled by edges. A D-type flip-flop captures the D input on its specified clock edge and stores it on Q until a relevant event changes it.
Where this model can mislead you
Real devices specify setup time, hold time and asynchronous controls. Input changes too close to the sampling edge can lead to metastability or unpredictable captured values.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Sequential circuits remember past conditions
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: At rising edges t1,t2,t3 the D input is 1,0,1.
A rising-edge D flip-flop will hold Q=1 after t1, Q=0 after t2, and Q=1 after t3, barring reset/set and timing violations.
Trace Q between edges as a flat stored state.
worked.conclusion: Q is stored and updates on the specified clock edge, not on every change of D.

pages.title: Counters turn clocks into state sequences
pages.text: A binary counter is a collection of state elements that progress through a sequence in response to input events.
pages.remember: 0000₂, because the fixed four-bit register cannot represent 16 and wraps modulo 16.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A binary counter is a collection of state elements that progress through a sequence in response to input events. A four-bit up-counter cycles 0000 to 1111 then wraps, representing 0 through 15 unsigned. A ripple counter propagates toggles between stages; a synchronous counter aligns updates to one clock and is often easier to time.
Where this model can mislead you
Counts depend on reset polarity, enable input and edge selection. Ripple outputs may briefly show intermediate codes; sample timing matters in downstream logic.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Counters turn clocks into state sequences

steps: Start a four-bit counter at 1110₂ (14).
Two valid rising edges produce 1111₂ (15) and then 0000₂ (0).
Sketch the carry to the most-significant bit and explain the difference between a planned wraparound and a random reset fault.
worked.conclusion: 0000₂, because the fixed four-bit register cannot represent 16 and wraps modulo 16.

reflection.ask: What value follows 1111₂ in a wrapping four-bit up-counter?
reflection.answer: 0000₂, because the fixed four-bit register cannot represent 16 and wraps modulo 16.

pages.title: Buses, clocks and digital-system timing
pages.text: A bus carries related signals between parts of a digital system.
pages.remember: No. Setup/hold constraints, propagation delays, skew and the chosen sampling edge determine the usable budget.
pages.sourceLesson: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A bus carries related signals between parts of a digital system. It may include multiple parallel data lines and control/clock lines; a serial bus sends bits sequentially. A clock coordinates events but does not automatically guarantee data validity: setup, hold, skew and propagation delays determine when a receiver can reliably sample a bit.
Where this model can mislead you
An apparent clean clock measured by a DMM can still contain jitter or missing edges. Use a properly configured scope or logic analyzer for time-related faults.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Buses, clocks and digital-system timing
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: A 1 MHz clock repeats once every 1/1,000,000 second = 1 μs.
A 20 ns propagation path consumes 2% of that period, but multiple stages, setup time and routing skew also count.
Draw clock edges and mark a valid data window rather than assuming the whole period is safe.
worked.conclusion: No. Setup/hold constraints, propagation delays, skew and the chosen sampling edge determine the usable budget.

reflection.ask: Does a 1 MHz clock mean every signal has 1 μs to settle?
reflection.answer: No. Setup/hold constraints, propagation delays, skew and the chosen sampling edge determine the usable budget.

pages.title: Input thresholds, hysteresis and undefined levels
pages.text: Digital inputs often have a region between guaranteed LOW and HIGH thresholds.
pages.remember: It sits in the undefined region, so the receiver has no guaranteed logical interpretation.
pages.sourceLesson: Real logic levels, pull resistors, debounce, and measurement

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

Digital inputs often have a region between guaranteed LOW and HIGH thresholds. A signal within that region should not be assumed either valid state. Schmitt-trigger inputs use different rising and falling switch thresholds, called hysteresis, to reduce chatter from slow or noisy edges. Correct logic levels depend on the actual device family and supply.
Where this model can mislead you
Threshold numbers here are examples only. Do not apply these limits to every 3.3 V part; manufacturer datasheets control and some inputs can be damaged by excess voltage.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Input thresholds, hysteresis and undefined levels
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: A 3.3 V digital input has guaranteed LOW at or below 0.8 V and HIGH at or above 2.0 V.
A measured 1.2 V is neither guaranteed; do not label it HIGH simply because it exceeds 1 V.
Identify the cause using a voltmeter and waveform observation.
worked.conclusion: It sits in the undefined region, so the receiver has no guaranteed logical interpretation.

reflection.ask: Why is 1.2 V problematic in a hypothetical input with VIL(max)=0.8 V and VIH(min)=2.0 V?
reflection.answer: It sits in the undefined region, so the receiver has no guaranteed logical interpretation.

pages.title: Floating inputs and defined states
pages.text: An unconnected high-impedance CMOS input can respond to noise, coupling or leakage because almost no external current is required to move its voltage.
pages.remember: Without an external or internal pull its voltage can float into undefined regions and create erratic switching.
pages.sourceLesson: Real logic levels, pull resistors, debounce, and measurement

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

An unconnected high-impedance CMOS input can respond to noise, coupling or leakage because almost no external current is required to move its voltage. A pull-up connects the node weakly to the positive rail; a pull-down connects it weakly to reference. These establish a default condition while allowing a stronger output or switch to override.
Where this model can mislead you
Pull resistors do not correct unsafe voltage differences or provide signal-level translation. Excessively weak pulls may allow slow edges, while overly strong ones waste current or overload drivers.

worked.conclusion: Without an external or internal pull its voltage can float into undefined regions and create erratic switching.

reflection.ask: Why does an unconnected CMOS input need a defined bias?

pages.title: Contact bounce as repeated logic edges
pages.text: A mechanical contact does not instantly settle; its surfaces touch and rebound over milliseconds, generating several rapid logic transitions.
pages.remember: Mechanical bouncing creates several transitions that an unfiltered digital circuit treats as separate edges.
pages.sourceLesson: Real logic levels, pull resistors, debounce, and measurement

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A mechanical contact does not instantly settle; its surfaces touch and rebound over milliseconds, generating several rapid logic transitions. A counter connected directly to a button may count each bounce as another press. Software timing, hardware RC filtering or a Schmitt-trigger conditioner can suppress unintended repeated events.
Where this model can mislead you
Debounce intervals are design-specific and must cover expected bounce and response-time needs. RC edges through an ordinary CMOS input can be slow; conditioning must match the input family.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Contact bounce as repeated logic edges
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: An up-counter increments five times for one press.
A scope shows rising transitions at 0,1,3,6,9 ms followed by stable HIGH.
A simple 20 ms confirmation interval after a detected transition could reject the extra bounces, if the actual interface requirements permit this delay.
worked.conclusion: Mechanical bouncing creates several transitions that an unfiltered digital circuit treats as separate edges.

reflection.ask: Why can one button press register as five increments?
reflection.answer: Mechanical bouncing creates several transitions that an unfiltered digital circuit treats as separate edges.

pages.title: Design and troubleshoot a debounced input
pages.text: A robust input has a known default state, suitable voltage/current levels, and deliberate treatment of contact bounce and electromagnetic noise.
pages.remember: The raw bouncing switch signal and the conditioned or debounced output, observed against the same time reference.
pages.sourceLesson: Real logic levels, pull resistors, debounce, and measurement

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A robust input has a known default state, suitable voltage/current levels, and deliberate treatment of contact bounce and electromagnetic noise. To diagnose repeats, observe the raw switch pin and the debounced signal separately rather than blaming firmware immediately. The same symptoms can arise from incorrect interrupt edge settings or input-pull configuration.
Where this model can mislead you
A delay-based debounce algorithm can miss legitimately rapid presses and add latency. Check the required human-machine response and test across switches and environmental conditions.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Design and troubleshoot a debounced input
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: A button with internal pull-up reads 1 when released, 0 when pressed.
If software triggers on falling edge, one press should produce one event.
With three falling edges during 8 ms, a 15 ms stable-state check may yield one accepted event.
Sketch the event count before and after filtering.
worked.conclusion: The raw bouncing switch signal and the conditioned or debounced output, observed against the same time reference.

reflection.ask: What two distinct signals would you measure to prove a debounce stage is working?
reflection.answer: The raw bouncing switch signal and the conditioned or debounced output, observed against the same time reference.

examples.title: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

detail.problem: Convert binary 1011 0110 to hex and decimal.
steps: Group into nibbles: 1011 and 0110.
1011₂ = B₁₆; 0110₂ = 6₁₆, so B6₁₆.
detail.answer: B6 hex and 182 decimal.
detail.transfer: A register value shown as 0xB6 can be decoded bit-by-bit using the same conversion.

examples.title: Binary, hexadecimal, gates, and sequential state

detail.problem: A register reads 0xB6. Convert it to binary and identify whether bits 7, 5, 3, and 0 are set.
steps: Bit positions from left are 7..0: 1 0 1 1 0 1 1 0.
Bits 7 and 5 are set; bit 3 is 0; bit 0 is 0.
detail.answer: 0xB6=10110110; bits 7 and 5 are set, bits 3 and 0 are clear.
detail.meaning: Hex-to-bit conversion is the basis of register masks and digital bus interpretation.

examples.title: Real logic levels, pull resistors, debounce, and measurement

detail.problem: A 3.3 V input with an internal pull-up reads random transitions when connected to a long unshielded wire and open switch.
steps: The default pull-up may be weak and the wire acts as an antenna/capacitor.
Verify the input voltage and transitions with a scope/logic analyzer.
Evaluate a suitable external pull-up, shorter routing, grounding, and debounce/filtering.
Check threshold and current requirements before selecting the resistor.
detail.answer: Treat this as signal-definition/noise/timing behavior, not a Boolean truth-table error.
detail.transfer: This is the same failure mode that can corrupt interrupt inputs and digital protocols.

examples.title: Real logic levels, pull resistors, debounce, and measurement

detail.problem: A pushbutton input uses a 10 kOhm pull-up to 3.3 V and shorts to ground when pressed. The input capacitance plus wiring is approximated as 100 pF. Estimate RC rise time scale after release and explain why real mechanical bounce is still much slower.
steps: The electrical pull-up edge from simple capacitance settles in a few microseconds.
Mechanical bounce can last milliseconds, thousands of times longer.
Therefore the pull-up alone defines the idle state but does not necessarily debounce the mechanical contact.
detail.answer: RC time scale is about 1 us; mechanical bounce remains a separate millisecond-scale phenomenon.
detail.meaning: Do not confuse electrical edge shaping from capacitance with actual mechanical contact bounce.

examples.title: Bit fields, ports, processors, and stored state

detail.problem: Register value is 0b10100101. Set bit 3 and clear bit 5 without changing others.
steps: Clear mask: ~(1<<5); AND clears bit 5.
0b10101101 with bit 5 cleared becomes 0b10001101.
Verify every unselected bit matches the original.
detail.transfer: The same pattern configures GPIO fields while preserving unrelated pins.

guided.text: Convert decimal 45 to binary and hex, then convert 0x3C back to binary and decimal.
Build a truth table for Y=(A AND B) OR (NOT C). Verify all eight combinations.
A D flip-flop samples on a rising edge. Explain what setup/hold means and why changing D at the same instant as the clock edge can produce an uncertain result.

questions.prompt: What is the output of a two-input AND gate for inputs 1 and 0?
questions.explanation: AND is high only when all inputs are high.

questions.prompt: What is the output of a two-input XOR gate for inputs 1 and 1?
choices: A stored copy of the previous input
questions.explanation: XOR is high for unequal input bits and low when they match.

questions.prompt: For an active-high NOR SR latch, S = 1 and R = 0 requests which state?
questions.explanation: The NOR SR latch is set by S high with R low. This convention differs from an active-low NAND latch; see the book errata.

questions.prompt: A binary counter has four flip-flops. How many distinct bit patterns can it represent?
questions.explanation: Four binary bits give 2⁴ = 16 possible states, normally 0 through 15 in an unsigned count.

questions.prompt: What must be compared before connecting outputs and inputs from different logic families?
choices: Guaranteed output levels, input thresholds and allowed voltages
Only the number of gates on a chip
Only whether both use binary symbols
questions.explanation: Binary names do not guarantee electrical compatibility. Datasheet limits control interfacing.

questions.prompt: Which stable-state output does NAND give for A=1,B=1?
questions.explanation: NAND complements the AND result, so 1 AND 1 becomes 0.

questions.prompt: How many rows are required for the complete three-input gate truth table?
questions.explanation: Two choices per input: 2³=8.

questions.prompt: A transmitter guarantees VOH(min)=2.4 V and receiver VIH(min)=2.0 V. What is HIGH noise margin?
questions.explanation: 2.4 V−2.0 V=0.4 V guaranteed HIGH margin.

questions.prompt: What is Q after a valid rising clock edge on a D flip-flop if D=0?
questions.explanation: A D flip-flop samples its D input at the specified active edge.

questions.prompt: What follows 1111₂ in a four-bit counter that wraps?
questions.explanation: The fixed-width four-bit count wraps modulo sixteen.

questions.prompt: A 2 MHz clock period is approximately what?
A counter records several presses for one physical button actuation. Which effect should you investigate first?
questions.explanation: Mechanical contacts bounce and can generate several digital transitions.

questions.prompt: What must a direct-driven seven-segment LED output provide?

pages.title: Start with a defensible fault model
pages.text: Digital troubleshooting starts from a symptom and an expected signal state under a recorded operating condition.
pages.remember: Because switch, power, firmware, output driver and load faults can produce the same symptom; choose a measurement that separates them.
pages.sourceLesson: Troubleshoot with competing hypotheses and high-information tests

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

Digital troubleshooting starts from a symptom and an expected signal state under a recorded operating condition. Divide the path into power, reference, source logic, connectors, destination logic and timing. Write two or three hypotheses whose predictions differ so each measurement has diagnostic value. This is more effective than touching every node at random.
Where this model can mislead you
A plausible hypothesis is not evidence of a failed part. If the circuit is unpowered or high-energy, assess safe access first; visual inspection and documentation may be the only permitted steps.

Measure in that sequence under one stable supply condition to divide causes efficiently.
worked.conclusion: Because switch, power, firmware, output driver and load faults can produce the same symptom; choose a measurement that separates them.

reflection.ask: Why is 'the MCU is bad' a weak first diagnosis when an indicator stays dark?
reflection.answer: Because switch, power, firmware, output driver and load faults can produce the same symptom; choose a measurement that separates them.

pages.title: Trace from last-good to first-bad
pages.text: A signal chain has checkpoints.
pages.remember: The adjacent points where one measured signal still matches expectation and the next does not, given controlled conditions.
pages.sourceLesson: Datasheet-to-wire integration and bus fault isolation

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A signal chain has checkpoints. When a known input enters a functioning block, there should be a predicted output at the next point. If a test point is correct and the following point is wrong, the fault has been narrowed to that stage or its loading and connections. Name the precise operating conditions and probe reference.
Where this model can mislead you
A downstream short can pull an upstream driver down, so 'last good' is not necessarily the only affected physical region. Loading and bidirectional lines complicate isolation.

pages.title: DMM, scope, logic probe and analyzer
pages.text: Choose a tool by the question.
pages.remember: A sufficiently fast oscilloscope with appropriate probe and trigger, not a basic DMM average or LED logic probe.
pages.sourceLesson: Measurement planning, probe discipline, and uncertainty

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

Choose a tool by the question. A DMM measures stable voltages and resistance; a scope reveals analog shape, edge rate and overshoot; a logic probe gives a quick threshold-based state/pulse clue; a logic analyzer records many digital transitions and event timing. No instrument can repair an undefined logic reference.
Where this model can mislead you
Logic analyzers may miss short glitches or analog overshoot because they quantize voltage; oscilloscopes require suitable bandwidth, coupling, grounding and rated probes.

worked.conclusion: A sufficiently fast oscilloscope with appropriate probe and trigger, not a basic DMM average or LED logic probe.

reflection.ask: Which instrument is most appropriate for seeing a 50 ns glitch on a digital line?
reflection.answer: A sufficiently fast oscilloscope with appropriate probe and trigger, not a basic DMM average or LED logic probe.

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

Every single-ended voltage measurement is a difference between a point and a reference. Good fault evidence includes circuit ID, supply condition, test-point name, reference, instrument settings, expected result and observed result. A screenshot without those details often cannot support a second technician reproducing the finding.

A benchtop scope ground clip may be earth bonded. Never attach it to a floating high-side or mains node without verifying safe measurement architecture and proper isolation equipment.

pages.title: Select a high-information test
pages.text: A useful diagnostic test splits possible causes.
pages.remember: Because an unpowered device may have no clock regardless of whether the root fault is a clock source or the missing supply.
pages.sourceLesson: Troubleshoot with competing hypotheses and high-information tests

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A useful diagnostic test splits possible causes. If every hypothesis predicts the same outcome, the reading adds little information. Trace supply and reference before spending time decoding protocol bytes. Use safe static checks and the simplest discriminating test that answers a specific question.
Where this model can mislead you
Do not inject pulses into an unknown node to 'see what happens.' First verify input rating, pin direction, known series protection and absence of conflicting outputs.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Select a high-information test
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: An output never toggles.
Three candidate causes are dead logic supply, missing input clock and output short.
A rail-voltage check distinguishes the first; a clock check distinguishes the second; a de-energized load isolation check can examine the third.
Choose the order that is safest and quickest.
worked.conclusion: Because an unpowered device may have no clock regardless of whether the root fault is a clock source or the missing supply.

reflection.ask: Why is measuring a clock line useful only after power is confirmed?
reflection.answer: Because an unpowered device may have no clock regardless of whether the root fault is a clock source or the missing supply.

pages.title: Logic probe fundamentals and thresholds
pages.text: A digital logic probe indicates HIGH, LOW and sometimes pulse activity using internal voltage comparators.
pages.remember: The instrument and the receiving IC can have different electrical thresholds and loading conditions.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A digital logic probe indicates HIGH, LOW and sometimes pulse activity using internal voltage comparators. Its results are meaningful only for a specified logic family, supply and reference. For a slow or stuck signal it can answer a quick state question; a variable-width pulse might not register reliably.
Where this model can mislead you
Probe current, capacitance and configuration may alter weak circuits. Treat a 'pulse' light as evidence to investigate waveform timing, not a complete frequency or protocol measurement.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Logic probe fundamentals and thresholds
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: A probe set for TTL thresholds lights HIGH at a pin while a 3.3 V CMOS receiver intermittently fails.
Measure actual voltage and compare it to that receiver's VIH requirement; the probe's own threshold does not certify receiving-device compatibility.
worked.conclusion: The instrument and the receiving IC can have different electrical thresholds and loading conditions.

reflection.ask: Why can a logic probe say HIGH when a receiving IC does not reliably read one?
reflection.answer: The instrument and the receiving IC can have different electrical thresholds and loading conditions.

pages.title: Logic pulser operation and precautions
pages.text: A logic pulser deliberately creates brief transitions on a test node for troubleshooting, usually under controlled low-voltage conditions.
pages.remember: Confirm the pin is an appropriate input, its voltage rating, reference, source loading, protection and the absence of another active driver.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A logic pulser deliberately creates brief transitions on a test node for troubleshooting, usually under controlled low-voltage conditions. It can help test a downstream logic path when the upstream signal source is absent, but only if the test point is truly appropriate for injection. Pull resistors, series protection, supply and fan-out govern safe use.
Where this model can mislead you

Never pulse two actively driven outputs against each other or use a pulser on mains, unknown bus voltages or safety-critical actuators. A simulated example is not permission for unsupervised injection.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Logic pulser operation and precautions
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: An isolated CMOS input is normally driven by a removable jumper.
With system power and connection strategy verified against manufacturer instructions, replace the jumper using a rated logic pulser and watch the downstream gate output change.
A response suggests the downstream combinational path is alive; it does not prove the original source works.
worked.conclusion: Confirm the pin is an appropriate input, its voltage rating, reference, source loading, protection and the absence of another active driver.

reflection.ask: What do you check before injecting a pulse on a digital input?
reflection.answer: Confirm the pin is an appropriate input, its voltage rating, reference, source loading, protection and the absence of another active driver.

pages.title: Pulse tracing and edge capture
pages.text: A pulsed stimulus propagates through logic after finite delay.
pages.remember: To prove whether each known stimulus produced the expected response, rather than comparing unsynchronized observations.
pages.sourceLesson: Datasheet-to-wire integration and bus fault isolation

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A pulsed stimulus propagates through logic after finite delay. Trace expected changes at successive points to identify a stage that stops responding. Use edge-triggering or digital analyzer capture when pulses are too short for a DMM. Capture both the excitation and response so a missing event can be tied to one stimulus.
Where this model can mislead you
A measured edge can be distorted by probe bandwidth, long ground lead and thresholds. Event correlation does not alone identify a failed part; check power, reset and configuration as well.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Pulse tracing and edge capture
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: A logic input pulses once every 10 ms.
TP1 follows every time, TP2 follows only half the events.
A two-channel scope capture with the same trigger shows which pulses fail, helping distinguish an intermittent enable from a missing edge.
worked.conclusion: To prove whether each known stimulus produced the expected response, rather than comparing unsynchronized observations.

reflection.ask: Why capture both pulser output and the next logic node at once?
reflection.answer: To prove whether each known stimulus produced the expected response, rather than comparing unsynchronized observations.

pages.title: Analyzer decoding, timing and false confidence
pages.text: A logic analyzer samples input voltage into digital states and can decode common protocols if threshold, sample rate, channel mapping and timing mode are correct.
pages.remember: Incorrect voltage threshold, sample rate, channel wiring/order and protocol/clock decoding settings.
pages.sourceLesson: Datasheet-to-wire integration and bus fault isolation

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A logic analyzer samples input voltage into digital states and can decode common protocols if threshold, sample rate, channel mapping and timing mode are correct. Decoding is an interpretation of captured edges. If those inputs are configured incorrectly, a plausible-looking data display can be wrong.
Where this model can mislead you

Even a high sample rate does not guarantee capture of all narrow glitches; logic threshold, probes, memory depth and trigger choice still matter. A scope can reveal the analog error behind digital decode symptoms.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Analyzer decoding, timing and false confidence
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: A 100 kHz square clock sampled at 150 kSa/s is too coarsely captured to reliably infer every edge.
Increase sample rate substantially above the fastest relevant transition pattern and confirm the timebase, channel polarity and decoder settings before calling the decoded address invalid.
worked.conclusion: Incorrect voltage threshold, sample rate, channel wiring/order and protocol/clock decoding settings.

reflection.ask: What four analyzer settings could create a false protocol error?
reflection.answer: Incorrect voltage threshold, sample rate, channel wiring/order and protocol/clock decoding settings.

pages.title: Layered fault diagnosis on a serial interface
pages.text: Digital communication can fail at several layers: unpowered device, wrong voltage thresholds, disconnected ground, missing clock/enable, framing mismatch or incorrect address/commands.
pages.remember: Supply and reference, voltage levels, pull-ups, clock and address correctness, then firmware setup.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

Digital communication can fail at several layers: unpowered device, wrong voltage thresholds, disconnected ground, missing clock/enable, framing mismatch or incorrect address/commands. Start from measured electrical behavior, then interpret protocol. I²C relies on shared open-drain lines and pull-ups; SPI uses explicit clock and chip selection; UART relies on agreed baud and framing.
Where this model can mislead you
Do not force 5 V pull-ups on a 3.3 V-only bus or probe high-energy unknown grounds. A decoder's NACK label is a symptom, not a certified root cause.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Layered fault diagnosis on a serial interface
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: An I²C device never acknowledges.
First check whether bus idle HIGH reaches a valid input threshold; then inspect START, address and ACK clock cycle.
A disconnected or unpowered target can produce NACK, but so can a wrong address or timing.
worked.conclusion: Supply and reference, voltage levels, pull-ups, clock and address correctness, then firmware setup.

reflection.ask: If a decoder shows NACK, what should you verify before blaming firmware?
reflection.answer: Supply and reference, voltage levels, pull-ups, clock and address correctness, then firmware setup.

pages.title: Signal-level compatibility and contention
pages.text: Two digital devices communicate only when their output levels, input thresholds, timing, direction and reference agree.
pages.remember: Guaranteed output and input thresholds, current limits, common reference and transient ratings control electrical compatibility.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

Two digital devices communicate only when their output levels, input thresholds, timing, direction and reference agree. Push-pull outputs actively drive high and low; connecting two such outputs together can create contention. Open-drain outputs sink current for zero and require a suitable pull-up to return high.
Where this model can mislead you
A common ground for low-voltage single-ended signals is not an instruction to tie together hazardous or isolated power systems. Different domains may require galvanic isolation instead.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Signal-level compatibility and contention
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: Device A can produce VOH(min)=2.4 V, while device B requires VIH(min)=2.0 V: guaranteed HIGH margin 0.4 V.
If B requires 3.0 V, the same link is not guaranteed.
Identify a level-translator or interface change before connecting mismatched pins.
worked.conclusion: Guaranteed output and input thresholds, current limits, common reference and transient ratings control electrical compatibility.

reflection.ask: Why is nominal 3.3 V versus 5 V insufficient to decide compatibility?
reflection.answer: Guaranteed output and input thresholds, current limits, common reference and transient ratings control electrical compatibility.

pages.title: Fault report and decision standard
pages.text: A useful fault report distinguishes an observed symptom, a tested hypothesis, actual measurements, root-cause evidence, corrective action and verification.
pages.remember: Repeatable expected behavior under documented test conditions, measurements and clear boundaries on what was and was not verified.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A useful fault report distinguishes an observed symptom, a tested hypothesis, actual measurements, root-cause evidence, corrective action and verification. It includes a limitation statement for anything not tested. In electronics service, 'it works now' is weaker than a repeatable acceptance test under defined operating conditions.
Where this model can mislead you
A single brief pass does not prove long-term reliability, heat tolerance or safe physical workmanship. Never infer professional qualification from a simulation or a multiple-choice exam.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Fault report and decision standard
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: Document a logic gate path that sometimes misses pulses: at 3.3 V and 1 kHz stimulus, 9 of 10 outputs arrived; after repairing one known loose connector, 100 of 100 observed pulses arrived.
Record setup, dates, scope trace names and which alternate conditions remain untested.
worked.conclusion: Repeatable expected behavior under documented test conditions, measurements and clear boundaries on what was and was not verified.

reflection.ask: What evidence supports closing a digital fault ticket?
reflection.answer: Repeatable expected behavior under documented test conditions, measurements and clear boundaries on what was and was not verified.

examples.title: Measurement planning, probe discipline, and uncertainty

detail.problem: A 100 mV ripple rides on a 5 V rail. The scope trace is off-screen at a sensitive vertical scale.
steps: Keep the ground clip on the approved circuit reference.
Start in DC coupling to confirm the 5 V level and safe signal range.
Use vertical position/offset or then AC coupling to examine the small ripple.
Enable an appropriate bandwidth limit if high-frequency noise is not the question.
Record that AC coupling removed the DC component; do not report the trace as absolute rail voltage.
detail.answer: Verify the DC level first, then isolate ripple with documented coupling and scale.
detail.transfer: This same sequence is used to characterize regulator ripple without losing the fact that a DC rail is present.

examples.title: Measurement planning, probe discipline, and uncertainty

detail.problem: A UART line should idle at 3.3 V and transmit bursts every second. A scope capture shows 2.1 V average with no obvious transitions.
steps: The word 'average' suggests the measurement may not be configured to reveal digital timing.
Verify the probe reference, attenuation, DC coupling, and vertical scale.
Set a time base that can show the 1 s burst interval or use single/normal trigger on an edge; then zoom into the bit timing.
If the line still sits near 2.1 V, investigate contention, wrong voltage domain, heavy loading, or incorrect pull network.
detail.answer: First prove the measurement setup can reveal the expected idle level and transitions, then treat a persistent 2.1 V level as an electrical fault symptom.
detail.meaning: A measurement plan separates 'the signal is wrong' from 'the observation method cannot show the signal.'

examples.title: Troubleshoot with competing hypotheses and high-information tests

detail.problem: A sensor returns no data. Its VDD is 0 V, upstream regulator output is 3.3 V, and continuity from regulator to connector is open.
steps: Firmware/protocol cannot work without sensor power.
The regulator is operating, so isolate the interconnect between rail and sensor connector.
Inspect fuse/link/trace/connector orientation and test continuity with power off.
Repair the confirmed open, then verify VDD and protocol response.
detail.answer: The evidence isolates an open power path upstream of the sensor.
detail.transfer: One causal chain avoids wasting time changing addresses or code before power exists.

examples.title: Troubleshoot with competing hypotheses and high-information tests

detail.problem: A sensor reads correctly over I2C until a motor is enabled, then NACKs occur. Hypotheses: supply noise, SDA/SCL electrical edge degradation, or firmware scheduling delay.
steps: Capture sensor rail and I2C lines during motor enable while logging firmware timing/error counters.
If rail dips below sensor limits at the exact NACK, supply integrity is supported.
If rail is stable but edges slow/ring or violate thresholds, electrical bus loading/noise is stronger.
If electrical signals are valid but transactions begin too late or timeout in software, scheduling/firmware becomes stronger.
detail.answer: Use synchronized electrical and software evidence so one event can separate power, signal-integrity, and firmware timing causes.
detail.meaning: A high-information test is designed around how candidate causes would look different.

examples.title: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

detail.problem: A 12-bit ADC with 3.3 V reference reports code 2048 on a 0–4095 scale. Estimate voltage.
steps: Voltage ≈ fraction × 3.3 V ≈ 1.65 V.
State the assumed code range/reference and expected quantization.
Compare with an independent meter measurement if available.
detail.answer: Approximately 1.65 V.
detail.transfer: A correct formula with the wrong reference or alignment still yields a believable wrong result.

guided.text: Write a measurement-plan row for checking a 3.3 V rail during MCU reset: quantity, expected range, instrument, connection, time resolution, and stop condition.
A meter reads 4.998 V three times on a nominal 5 V rail. Explain what you can and cannot claim without the meter accuracy specification and system tolerance.
For a suspected 20 us glitch, explain why a DMM may miss the event and choose scope settings that would make the event observable.
Rewrite three vague hypotheses into testable statements with predicted observations.
For a four-stage signal chain, choose a half-split measurement and explain what each possible result tells you about the remaining search space.
Given one intermittent failure, state how you would preserve configuration, trigger/capture evidence, and avoid changing multiple variables before reproduction.

teachBack: Explain how you turn a troubleshooting question into a reproducible measurement plan. Distinguish accuracy, resolution, repeatability, and loading using one real instrument example.

Take a no-output or bus-failure example and teach how to create three competing hypotheses, select one high-information test, interpret each possible outcome, and avoid confusing symptom with root cause.
Compare UART, I2C, and SPI electrically and logically. Then explain one I2C rise-time failure and one SPI CPOL/CPHA failure using what you would expect to see on a scope or logic analyzer.

Choose an I2C or SPI device and teach the path from datasheet pin/timing requirements to wiring, MCU configuration, first transaction, analyzer capture, register interpretation, and one layered fault diagnosis.

questions.prompt: What makes a scope screenshot reproducible evidence?
choices: The measured value plus test point, reference, probe/coupling/timebase/scale, and expected behavior
A phone photo with no labels
questions.explanation: Correct. Context and settings let another person reconstruct and judge the measurement.

questions.prompt: Which statement is a defensible root cause?
choices: An open connector pin removed sensor VDD; continuity and voltage evidence identified it, and repair restored both rail and data
questions.explanation: Correct. It names the mechanism, evidence, correction, and verified effect.

questions.prompt: What creates the high level on a standard I²C bus?
choices: Pull-up resistors return released open-drain lines high
questions.explanation: Correct. Devices actively pull low and release; pull-ups establish high.

questions.prompt: The analyzer decodes no I²C traffic and both lines remain low. What should be checked first?
choices: Electrical power, shorts, pull-ups, and whether a device is holding the lines
questions.explanation: Correct. A physically stuck bus must be resolved before transaction parsing.

questions.prompt: Which is the most useful first test for an entirely unresponsive digital board?
choices: Inject a pulse into any node
Confirm intended supply and reference under known conditions
questions.explanation: A missing rail explains many missing edges and must be checked before diagnosis.

questions.prompt: You must observe a 50 ns glitch on a digital line. Best instrument?
choices: Suitable oscilloscope with bandwidth and triggering
questions.explanation: A scope with sufficient bandwidth/timebase can show the analog shape of the short glitch.

questions.prompt: What determines whether a probe reports a valid logic HIGH?
choices: Its logic threshold and correct reference
The text of a register name alone
questions.explanation: Probe indications depend on configured comparator thresholds and reference.

questions.prompt: Before using a logic pulser, which condition is essential?
choices: Confirmed input rating and no contending output
questions.explanation: Controlled injection requires safe low-voltage input, correct levels and no driven-output conflict.

questions.prompt: An input pulse reaches TP1 but none arrive at TP2. Which conclusion is strongest?
choices: Fault region is narrowed to stage/path between TP1 and TP2
Every device on the board is broken
questions.explanation: Last-good/first-bad boundary localizes the missing transition under a known stimulus.

questions.prompt: A protocol decoder shows errors at an inadequate sample rate. What should you do?
choices: Reconfigure sample rate, threshold and decoder first
questions.explanation: Incorrect acquisition settings can create convincing but false digital decoding.

questions.prompt: Which evidence most strongly supports digital fault closure?
choices: Repeated measurements under defined conditions and recorded limitations
questions.explanation: Reproducible expected behavior, setup details and limitations substantiate fault isolation.

pages.title: An interface is a complete agreement
pages.text: An electronic interface is more than a connector shape.
pages.remember: It does not establish compatible signal voltages, pinout, timing, direction, power or protocol.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

An electronic interface is more than a connector shape. Two devices must agree on physical voltage/current limits, signal direction, reference, timing, pin assignments, and protocol meaning. A cable that fits can still connect incompatible signal standards. Good technicians identify both endpoints and draw a signal/power map before making a connection.
Where this model can mislead you
Label similarity never certifies compatibility. Do not connect unknown power systems to establish ground, especially when isolation or hazardous mains may be involved.

worked.heading: Reason it through · An interface is a complete agreement
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: A sensor produces 5 V push-pull data and a processor pin accepts 3.3 V maximum.
Although both are labeled 'digital', the link is unsafe without a suitable level-shifting or replacement interface.
Record voltage limits, active driver directions, logic thresholds and common reference first.
worked.conclusion: It does not establish compatible signal voltages, pinout, timing, direction, power or protocol.

reflection.ask: Why is a matching connector not proof that two products can communicate?
reflection.answer: It does not establish compatible signal voltages, pinout, timing, direction, power or protocol.

pages.text: To verify a logic link, compare the transmitter's guaranteed HIGH/LOW outputs with receiver's VIH and VIL input thresholds.

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

To verify a logic link, compare the transmitter's guaranteed HIGH/LOW outputs with receiver's VIH and VIL input thresholds. Check maximum input voltage and whether outputs can source or sink required current. Translation may need one-way buffered conversion, bidirectional open-drain shifters or galvanic isolation depending on line behavior.
Where this model can mislead you
A resistor divider might work for some unidirectional slow signals but is not a universal translator; RC loading, speed and back-power paths matter.

pages.title: Grounding, isolation and signal return
pages.text: Every single-ended signal needs an electrical return path, but the correct reference may be signal ground, chassis, protective earth or an isolated domain.
pages.remember: The receiving device may not share an appropriate reference or may have incompatible electrical thresholds or baud/format settings.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

Every single-ended signal needs an electrical return path, but the correct reference may be signal ground, chassis, protective earth or an isolated domain. Those are different safety and noise functions. A ground offset between systems can corrupt communication or create dangerous currents. Isolation breaks a conductive path while preserving information transfer through rated components.
Where this model can mislead you
Never defeat protective earth or join unknown grounds merely to remove noise. A bench scope ground lead can create a short across an unintended potential difference.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Grounding, isolation and signal return

steps: Two boards communicate over 3.3 V UART but share no suitable signal reference; data appears intermittent.
Draw TX, RX and their return path.
If both are safe common low-voltage domains, a shared reference may be appropriate; if one is isolated or mains-related, use a correctly rated isolator instead.
worked.conclusion: The receiving device may not share an appropriate reference or may have incompatible electrical thresholds or baud/format settings.

reflection.ask: Why can UART signals fail even when TX toggles correctly?
reflection.answer: The receiving device may not share an appropriate reference or may have incompatible electrical thresholds or baud/format settings.

pages.title: Signal conflicts and what symptoms mean
pages.text: Signals can conflict because of electrical contention, simultaneous transmitters, different output types, timing mismatch or ground disturbance.
pages.remember: Unexpected intermediate/stuck voltage with excess current or heating, especially when output commands differ.
pages.sourceLesson: Media, connectors, signal paths, and optical fundamentals

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

Signals can conflict because of electrical contention, simultaneous transmitters, different output types, timing mismatch or ground disturbance. Symptoms include stuck rails, overheating, garbled bytes, intermittent resets, missing ACKs or distorted edges. The diagnosis depends on the topology, not the label of the interface.
Where this model can mislead you
A logic line stuck low can also be an intentionally asserted active-low control, disconnected supply or open-drain pull-down. Confirm expected state before describing contention.

worked.heading: Reason it through · Signal conflicts and what symptoms mean
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: Two push-pull outputs are wired together; one drives HIGH and the other LOW.
The resulting high current can pull the line into an invalid level and damage a device.
A first safe step is de-energize, map drivers, and correct the wiring rather than force a pulse to override the line.
worked.conclusion: Unexpected intermediate/stuck voltage with excess current or heating, especially when output commands differ.

reflection.ask: What symptom suggests two push-pull outputs may be fighting?
reflection.answer: Unexpected intermediate/stuck voltage with excess current or heating, especially when output commands differ.

pages.title: UART, RS-232 and USB are not interchangeable
pages.text: A UART peripheral formats serial bits with start, data, optional parity and stop intervals.
pages.remember: The voltage levels/polarity and sometimes electrical characteristics differ; a rated transceiver is required.
pages.sourceLesson: UART frames, parameters, levels, and error causes

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

A UART peripheral formats serial bits with start, data, optional parity and stop intervals. MCU UART pins commonly use logic-level voltage. Traditional RS-232 is a different electrical signaling standard, and USB uses its own signaling, enumeration and protocol roles. A USB cable cannot directly substitute for the required interface translator.
Where this model can mislead you
Some modern connectors use atypical pinouts and voltage levels. Never assume polarity or pinout based on the presence of a DB9, USB-C or header connector.

worked.heading: Reason it through · UART, RS-232 and USB are not interchangeable
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: A 9600 bit/s UART has nominal bit duration 1/9600≈104.2 μs.
For an 8-N-1 frame, ten bits (start + eight data + stop) require about 1.042 ms per character before gaps.
A 5 V RS-232-style converter or USB bridge is not selected without checking its exact endpoint specification.
worked.conclusion: The voltage levels/polarity and sometimes electrical characteristics differ; a rated transceiver is required.

reflection.ask: Why isn't an MCU UART TX pin safe to wire straight to a conventional RS-232 port?
reflection.answer: The voltage levels/polarity and sometimes electrical characteristics differ; a rated transceiver is required.

pages.title: I²C open-drain operation and pull-ups
pages.text: I²C uses SDA for data and SCL for clock, with participants commonly able to pull each line LOW or release it.
pages.remember: Open-drain participants sink current for LOW; the resistor establishes HIGH when drivers release the line.
pages.sourceLesson: Interface roles, signaling, and conversion

paragraphs: The physical model and meaning

I²C uses SDA for data and SCL for clock, with participants commonly able to pull each line LOW or release it. A pull-up resistor returns a released line HIGH, and device addresses select a target. A valid bus requires voltage compatibility, enough sink capability, acceptable capacitance/rise time and correct timing.
Where this model can mislead you
A shared I²C bus must not be tied to unsafe pull-up voltage. Address scanners do not prove all device features work, and many I²C configurations differ in speed and addressing.

worked.heading: Reason it through · I²C open-drain operation and pull-ups
worked.scenario: Predict the result before reading each reasoned step.
steps: With a 3.3 V bus, 4.7 kΩ pull-up and line held LOW at near zero, the pull-up current is approximately 3.3/4700=0.70 mA.
When released, bus capacitance charges through the resistor; larger capacitance lengthens rise time.
Observe START as SDA falling while SCL is HIGH.
worked.conclusion: Open-drain participants sink current for LOW; the resistor establishes HIGH when drivers release the line.

reflection.ask: Why do SDA and SCL normally require pull-up resistance?
reflection.answer: Open-drain participants sink current for LOW; the resistor establishes HIGH when drivers release the line.
